scope: Exact two-file source check for one externally limited 120-second, two-condition numeric replay. No replay execution, model action, numeric tensor body read or RGB read performed by this reviewer.
checks: Exact author-supplied replay/protocol SHA and 0444 modes match; original pipeline SHA and archived event-file SHA independently match.

Syntax compilation only succeeded for replay and exact extracted AST. Three unique undecorated original methods are selected; nested polygon helper retained. No pipeline module import or model construction is present. Renderer uses only numerical globals and surfel position/normal/radius; retrieval uses source mapping and context_num_frames=4.

Pinned seq58/60/62 metadata contains numeric tensors/scalars/containers only. Tensor decode permits float32/float64/int32/int64 under archive/tensors/*.bin with byte-length and bytes-SHA checks. Exact selected metadata has no image or RGB tree; outputs are numeric depth/index/cos NPZ and receipt.

For s>0, scaling world position X, camera translation t and radius by s with fixed R gives R^-1(sX-st)=s R^-1(X-t); perspective x/z and y/z are unchanged. Normal orientation and source mapping remain unchanged. Focal lengths/principal point and image dimensions are retained. The source enforces the stated center-projection tolerance.

Median positive camera-z selects one length scale before either normalized rasterization result, without searching factors. The original-unit condition uses original surfels and numerically unchanged float64 camera; checks each saved numerical output with array_equal and retrieval equality before the second condition.

Original near/far constants 0.1/1000, rasterization constants and retrieval weight cos/(1+depth) remain unchanged. Therefore scale dependence is expected to test absolute numerical assumptions; this comparison alone does not isolate near-plane clipping from all other dimensional constants or establish physical calibration.

Exactly two conditions are enumerated. execution_01 is create-only and currently absent; successful output paths are unique per condition, plus receipt, then chmod0444. A failure leaves its consumed directory. No loop retries or alternate scale search appear.
The 120-second limit is an external runner obligation stated by protocol; replay.py has no internal timeout. This review does not attest that an outer timed run occurred.

All result claims explicitly remain post-exposure numerical diagnostics: second_generation_batch_run=false, c2_complete=false, new_method_validated=false; no complete C2, baseline success, quality improvement or novelty claim is authorized.
